class.name: GDScript
class.brief_description: A script implemented in the GDScript programming language.
class.description:
A script implemented in the GDScript programming language, saved with the [code].gd[/code] extension. The script extends the functionality of all objects that instantiate it. Calling [method new] creates a new instance of the script. [method Object.set_script] extends an existing object, if that object's class matches one of the script's base classes. If you are looking for GDScript's built-in functions, see [@GDScript] instead. [b]Strict type analysis:[/b] GDScript supports nullable annotations, typed callable and signal signatures, and nested typed containers. Nullable object types use [code]T?[/code], while plain [code]T[/code] can be checked as non-nullable when [member ProjectSettings.debug/gdscript/analysis/strict_null_checks] is enabled. [Callable] and [Signal] signatures can be written as [code]Callable[[ArgType, ...], ReturnType][/code] and [code]Signal[[ArgType, ...]][/code]. [Array] and [Dictionary] annotations can contain nested typed containers such as [code]Dictionary[String, Array[int]][/code]. [codeblock] signal renamed_to(new_name: String)
func get_target() -> Node?: return null
func accept_target(target: Node) -> void: pass
func name_length(name: String) -> int: return name.length()
func on_renamed(new_name: String) -> void: pass
func get_dynamic_value() -> Variant: return 1
func use_strict_types() -> void: var maybe_target: Node? = get_target() if maybe_target != null: accept_target(maybe_target)
var callback: Callable[[String], int] = name_length var length: int = callback.call("Player")
var renamed: Signal[[String]] = renamed_to renamed.connect(on_renamed) renamed.emit("Player")
var scores: Dictionary[String, Array[int]] = { "level_1": [10, 20, 30], } print(length, scores["level_1"][0])
# Rejected when strict_null_checks is enabled: # accept_target(get_target())
# Rejected when strict_dynamic_checks is enabled: # var typed_value: int = get_dynamic_value() [/codeblock] Most callable and signal signature checks run as part of normal static analysis. [member ProjectSettings.debug/gdscript/analysis/strict_dynamic_checks] adds stricter checks at dynamic boundaries by rejecting [Variant] values where a non-[Variant] static type is required. [b]Generics:[/b] classes and methods can be parameterized by one or more type parameters, declared with the same bracket convention used by [Array] and [Dictionary]. A type parameter is written after the class or method name ([code]class Box[T][/code], [code]func swap[T](...)[/code]), and the parameter is then usable as a type inside the body. [codeblock] # Generic class: `T` types members and method signatures. class Box[T]: var value: T
func set_value(new_value: T) -> void: value = new_value
func get_value() -> T: return value
# A generic class can also be file-level with `class_name Box[T]`.
# Generic method, independent of any class type parameter. func swap[T](a: T, b: T) -> Array[T]: return [b, a] [/codeblock] [b]Use-site type arguments:[/b] a generic class is specialized by supplying type arguments in brackets at the use site, including for construction: [code]Box[int].new()[/code]. A generic method infers its type parameters from the argument types, and explicit application is available as a fallback ([code]swap[float](1, 2)[/code]). Inference fails with an error directing you to apply the arguments explicitly when arguments conflict (for example [code]swap(1, "x")[/code]) or when a parameter is unconstrained because it appears only in the return type. Multiple parameters ([code]Pair[K, V][/code]) and multi-argument application ([code]Pair[int, String].new()[/code]) are supported. [codeblock] var box := Box[int].new() box.set_value(42) # Accepts `int`. var n: int = box.get_value() # `get_value()` is substituted to `-> int`.
var inferred := swap(1, 2) # `T` inferred as `int`. var explicit := swap[float](1, 2) # `T` applied explicitly. [/codeblock] [b]Bounds:[/b] a type parameter can declare an upper bound with [code]T: Bound[/code]. The bound may be a class ([code]Box[T: RefCounted][/code]) or a trait ([code]Box[T: Damageable][/code]). A type argument must satisfy the bound (be the bound, derive from it, or — for a trait bound — [code]uses[/code] it), and inside the body a [code]T[/code]-typed value exposes the bound type's members for static checking. Bounds are matched [i]invariantly[/i] in their own type arguments: [code]Stack[String][/code] does not satisfy a [code]List[int][/code] bound. [codeblock] trait Damageable: @abstract func take_damage(amount: int) -> void
class Box[T: Damageable]: var value: T
func hit() -> void: value.take_damage(5) # `Damageable` members resolve on `T`. [/codeblock] [b]Inheritance:[/b] a class can extend a generic base, rebinding the base's parameter to its own ([code]class Stack[U] extends List[U][/code]) or fixing it to a concrete type ([code]class IntList extends List[int][/code]). Inherited members and method signatures are substituted along the chain. Generic specialization is [i]invariant[/i]: [code]Stack[String][/code] is a [code]List[String][/code], not a [code]List[int][/code]. The F-bounded / CRTP pattern [code]class Sword extends Box[Sword][/code] is supported. [b]Reified runtime model:[/b] generic [i]class instances[/i] are [i]reified[/i] — their type arguments survive to runtime. A [code]Box[int][/code] instance carries its bound type arguments, and writes to a [code]T[/code]-typed member are validated against them exactly as [Array] element insertion is, so assigning an incompatible value through a dynamic reference fails at runtime (values that convert, such as a [float] written to an [code skip-lint]int[/code] slot, are coerced). The reified arguments round-trip through [code].tres[/code]/scene save-load, resource duplication, and hot-reload. A generic class named without type arguments is a [i]raw[/i] generic (like an untyped [Array]): [code]var b: Box[/code] is a permissive supertype that any [code]Box[X][/code] assigns to, and its members are dynamic, with writes still validated against the instance's reified argument at runtime. Generic [i]methods[/i], by contrast, are a static inference and checking device: their type parameters are [i]not[/i] reified and are erased at runtime. A generic method that returns a container whose element is a type parameter ([code]func singleton[T](...) -> Array[T][/code]) produces an untyped array at runtime; the element type is recovered from the target's concrete type at the assignment site, so assigning the result to an [code]Array[int][/code] retypes it while assigning to an untyped [Array] leaves it untyped. [b]Generic traits:[/b] traits can be generic ([code]trait Holder[T][/code]) and applied with type arguments ([code]class IntBox uses Holder[int][/code]); conformance is checked under substitution, so the implementation must satisfy every required member with the argument applied. Traits can also require generic methods ([code]@abstract func transform[U](value: U) -> Array[U][/code]), which an implementation satisfies up to type-parameter renaming (alpha-equivalence by ordinal position). [b]Reflection:[/b] generic type information is available at runtime. [method is_generic] and [method get_type_parameter_list] report a class's declared type parameters (as [GDScriptTypeParameter] descriptors), and [method GDScriptReflection.get_type_arguments] returns the reified type arguments bound onto an instance.

method.name: get_type_parameter_list
method.description: Returns the generic type parameters declared directly on this script's class, in declaration order, as an array of [GDScriptTypeParameter] descriptors. Returns an empty array for non-generic classes. This is part of the runtime reflection surface for GDScript generics. [codeblock] # class Box[T]: ... var Box = load("box.gd") for parameter in Box.get_type_parameter_list(): print(parameter.name) # Prints &"T" [/codeblock]

method.name: is_generic
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this script's class declares one or more generic type parameters (for example [code]class Box[T][/code]). See [method get_type_parameter_list].
